content.title: About
content.content: Peanuts (Arachis hypogaea) are the edible seeds of a plant native to South America. Although they are commonly called nuts, peanuts are legumes, related to beans and lentils. They have a rich, savory flavor and are eaten roasted, boiled, or ground into peanut butter and are used in cooking in many cuisines.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Peanuts are legumes, not true tree nuts.
The plant flowers above ground, but the pods develop underground.
Peanuts originated in South America and spread around the world after European contact.
Peanut butter is one of the most popular peanut products.
Peanuts are also pressed to make peanut oil.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: Peanuts provide a good amount of protein for a plant food.

items.title: Provides healthy fats
items.content: Peanuts contain mostly unsaturated fats, which can be part of a heart-friendly diet.

items.title: Contains niacin, folate, and vitamin E
items.content: These nutrients support energy metabolism, cell function, and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Provides magnesium and fiber
items.content: These support normal muscle function and digestion.

items.title: Contains plant compounds
items.content: Peanuts contain polyphenols such as resveratrol, which has antioxidant properties.

items.title: Peanut allergy
items.content: Peanut allergy is one of the more common and serious food allergies and can cause severe reactions. People with this allergy must avoid peanuts and check labels carefully.

items.title: Aflatoxin
items.content: Peanuts can be contaminated with aflatoxin, a toxin produced by mold, especially when stored improperly.

items.title: High in calories and added salt
items.content: Peanuts are calorie-dense, and salted or flavored varieties can be high in sodium.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: Whole peanuts are not suitable for young children because they can cause choking.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Peanuts can be eaten roasted or boiled as a snack, added to salads, stir-fries, sauces, and baked goods, or ground into peanut butter. Choose unsalted or lightly salted peanuts and peanut butter without added sugar when possible.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store shelled peanuts in an airtight container in a cool, dry place, or in the refrigerator for longer storage. Keep peanuts in the shell in a cool, dry place. Discard peanuts that look moldy, shriveled, or smell musty or rancid. Natural peanut butter is best refrigerated after opening.
